title: popup-window: window.open() opens a plain native window (no browser address bar) — vendored webview patch

decisions.text: Patch the vendored webview C++ backend (win32_edge.hh), not Pascal. A NewWindowRequested handler must be a real COM object plus a second CreateCoreWebView2Controller round-trip; with the official WebView2.h already fetched by the build this is ~350 lines of natural C++, while a raw-vtable Pascal implementation (the AppMain.openDevTools trick) would need hand-built COM objects, IIDs and interface layouts — bigger and more brittle. Requested by/for KKMindWave panel-window PW4.2 (owner confirmed the default popup shows an address bar in the exe, 2026-07-13).

The popup controller is created from the SAME ICoreWebView2Environment (ICoreWebView2_2::get_Environment of the opener) — same user-data folder and same browser process, so BroadcastChannel/localStorage/window.close() between opener and popup keep working exactly as with the default popup. On any early takeover failure (e.g. no ICoreWebView2_2 on an ancient runtime) the request is left unhandled and the default popup (with its address bar) still opens — a degraded window beats a lost one.

Pinning the patch: webview/ is a NESTED git clone of upstream (own .git), so the outer repo cannot track its files (git add -f is a no-op). Pinned twice instead: (1) a commit on the appcore-patches branch INSIDE the nested webview repo (rebase over upstream on refresh); (2) docs/popup-window/win32_edge-newwindow.patch in the outer AppCore repo (git apply from webview/ if the clone is ever lost). All patch sites carry AppCore patch (KKMindWave panel-window...) comments.

steps.title: win32_edge.hh: webview2_popup_window + webview2_new_window_handler + engine wiring
artifacts: webview2_popup_event_handler<T>: tiny COM adapter for the (ICoreWebView2*, IUnknown*) events (DocumentTitleChanged / WindowCloseRequested)

webview2_popup_window: bare WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW (title bar only), controller from the opener's environment, GetDeferral + put_NewWindow + put_Handled(TRUE); WindowFeatures size/pos honored (AdjustWindowRect for content-size); document.title -> caption; window.close() -> DestroyWindow; WM_SIZE -> put_Bounds; WM_DESTROY -> controller Close + release; icons inherited from the opener (WM_GETICON); apply_window_theme on the popup
webview2_new_window_handler subscribed in embed() after settings; removed + released in the engine destructor

PW4.1 geometry follow-up: features left/top are treated as the desired CONTENT top-left; the frame is offset by the non-client margins (frame.left/top from AdjustWindowRect) so the content lands there — repeated detach/reopen is drift-free (the child persists/reads window.screenX/screenY)
